newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIAN LOWER YIELDS VS US APPROPRIATE-RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIAN LOWER YIELDS VS US APPROPRIATE-RBA.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Ian Macfarlane said on Tuesday that it was entirely appropriate that Australia should have a lower interest rate regime than the United States, given that the two countries were at different positions in the economic cycle.
He also said he believed these lower interest rates were a substantial benefit to the Australian economy.

"We now have lower interest rates out to five years than the United States ... This is entirely fit and proper, given the different cyclical positions of the two economies and given our lower inflation," Macfarlane told a conference in Perth.

Australia's official interest rates were cut to 5.0 percent last month. U.S. Federal Funds are currently at 5.5 percent while Australian three-year bonds yields are currently trading at around 5.74 percent versus 6.20 percent in the U.S. Five-year yields are around parity at about 6.20 percent.

"It would have been unthinkable even a few years ago," Macfarlane said. "Financial markets took it for granted that Australia would always be a high interest country relative to the United States," he said.
He said international investors put Australia in with a group of countries known as "high yielders".
"I am strongly of the view that these lower interest rates are a substantial benefit for Australian businesses," he added.
